# SPI Host FSM Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

This module is the command/control core of an SPI host. It accepts command-segment descriptors, applies the associated SPI configuration, and generates the serial-clock, chip-select, serial-data direction, and data-path control behaviors needed to execute each segment.

The module must:

- generate the SPI serial clock with the configured polarity, phase, and divider;
- assert and deassert the correct chip-select lines with the configured lead, trail, and idle timing;
- control whether the serial data outputs are enabled for standard, dual, or quad transfers;
- indicate when transmit bytes should be loaded, when received bytes should be captured, and when the serial data should shift;
- stall cleanly when transmit data is not available or receive data cannot be accepted;
- support back-to-back command segments without raising chip-select when the segment descriptor requests chip-select hold.

The module is parameterized by the number of chip-select lines. It shall support one or more chip-select outputs.

---

## 2. Command Segment Model

Each command segment is described by:

- a segment length;
- a transfer speed: standard, dual, or quad;
- a direction: dummy, receive-only, transmit-only, or bidirectional;
- a chip-select hold flag, indicating whether the chip-select remains asserted after the segment;
- the target chip-select ID;
- configuration settings for the target device: clock polarity, clock phase, full-cycle sampling, clock divider, and chip-select timing counts.

The segment length is encoded such that a value of zero means one byte-time or one dummy-cycle time. In general, the number of byte-times or dummy cycles in a segment equals the encoded length plus one.

The direction and speed determine whether data is transmitted, received, or neither:

- Dummy: no transmit data and no received data; only clock cycles are generated.
- Receive-only: no serial-data outputs are enabled; received data is read out at byte boundaries.
- Transmit-only: serial-data outputs are enabled according to speed; no received data is read.
- Bidirectional: transmit and receive happen at the same time. This is only valid at standard speed.

---

## 3. Reset and Enable Behavior

### 3.1 Hardware Reset

On hardware reset, the module shall:

- place the command sequencer in its initial idle state;
- deassert all chip-select outputs;
- drive the serial clock to its idle level;
- disable all serial-data output enables;
- suppress all data-path strobes;
- assert command ready, so that a command can be accepted.

### 3.2 Software Reset

When the software reset input is asserted, the module shall abandon the current segment and return to its initial idle state. Any in-progress chip-select hold, clock generation, or data transfer activity shall be terminated.

The module shall indicate completion of the reset by returning the active indicator low and by deasserting all chip-select outputs.

### 3.3 Module Enable

When the main enable is deasserted, the module shall suspend operation in its current state. It shall not generate further serial-clock edges, data strobes, or chip-select transitions. When the enable is reasserted, operation shall resume from the suspended point.

---

## 4. Serial Clock Generation

The serial clock must be generated with the polarity and timing selected by the active configuration.

### 4.1 Clock Polarity

- When the configured polarity is 0, the serial clock is idle low and produces positive pulses.
- When the configured polarity is 1, the serial clock is idle high and produces negative pulses.

The idle level is maintained whenever no command segment is actively transferring data, including lead, trail, idle, and configuration-switch periods.

### 4.2 Clock Divider

The serial clock frequency is derived from the module’s input clock using a clock divider setting.

Each half-period of the serial clock shall have a duration of:

```text
(clock_divider_setting + 1) input clock cycles
```

Therefore the full serial clock period is:

```text
2 * (clock_divider_setting + 1) input clock cycles
```

When the clock divider setting is zero, the serial clock toggles at half the input clock frequency.

### 4.3 Clock Activity

The serial clock shall only toggle while the module is executing the active portion of a command segment.

The serial clock shall not toggle:

- while all chip-select outputs are high;
- during the chip-select lead period;
- during the chip-select trail period;
- during the chip-select idle period;
- during a stall;
- while the module is disabled.

---

## 5. Chip-Select Control

The chip-select outputs are active-low. Exactly one chip-select line shall be asserted during a transaction, selected by the command’s chip-select ID. All other chip-select outputs shall remain high.

### 5.1 Normal Single-Segment Sequence

For a normal segment with chip-select hold disabled, the chip-select behavior shall be:

1. At the start of the command, the selected chip-select is asserted low.
2. The serial clock remains idle for the configured lead time.
3. The serial clock toggles for the required number of data or dummy cycles.
4. After the last clock edge, the serial clock returns to its idle level.
5. The selected chip-select remains low for the configured trail time.
6. The selected chip-select is deasserted high.
7. All chip-select lines remain high for the configured idle time before the next command starts.

### 5.2 Lead, Trail, and Idle Timing

The lead, trail, and idle delays are expressed in serial-clock half-periods.

- Lead delay from chip-select assertion low to the first serial-clock edge:
  ```text
  (lead_setting + 1) half-periods
  ```
- Trail delay from the last serial-clock edge to chip-select deassertion high:
  ```text
  (trail_setting + 1) half-periods
  ```
- Idle delay while all chip-selects are high between transactions:
  ```text
  (idle_setting + 1) half-periods
  ```

These are minimum delays. The module shall not end any of these periods before the corresponding count has elapsed.

### 5.3 Chip-Select Hold After a Segment

If the chip-select hold flag is asserted for a segment, the module shall keep the selected chip-select low after the final serial-clock edge, instead of performing the normal trail and deassertion sequence.

When holding chip-select active, the module may do one of the following:

- If the next command for the same chip-select ID is already available, begin the next segment immediately on the next serial-clock half-period, without an intervening trail, idle, or lead delay.
- If no command is available, wait in an idle state with the chip-select still asserted low. In this state, command ready shall be asserted so that a new segment can be accepted.
- If a command arrives while waiting with chip-select asserted, and it selects the same chip-select ID, start that segment without deasserting the chip-select.
- If a command arrives while waiting with chip-select asserted, but it selects a different chip-select ID, the module shall first close out the previous transaction: apply the trail delay, deassert the old chip-select, apply the idle delay, then assert the new chip-select and apply the lead delay. The new command shall only be acknowledged after the old transaction has been properly terminated.

### 5.4 Back-to-Back Segments

When a segment with chip-select hold enabled is followed by another segment for the same chip-select and no configuration change is required, the module shall not insert any extra chip-select idle time between the two segments. The chip-select remains low from the first segment into the next.

---

## 6. Configuration Changes

The module shall latch the active configuration when a command is accepted.

When a new command is accepted from a condition in which all chip-select outputs are high, and the command’s configuration differs from the latched configuration, the module shall not begin the new command immediately. Instead, it shall hold all chip-select outputs high for an additional idle period before starting the next transaction.

This configuration-switch delay ensures that clock polarity, clock phase, clock divider, and other timing settings are changed only while no chip-select is asserted and no device is being clocked.

If the configuration is unchanged, the normal chip-select idle-to-lead sequence shall be used.

---

## 7. Serial Data Output Enable Control

The module shall control whether the serial data line output drivers are enabled.

- When all chip-select outputs are high, all serial-data output enables shall be off.
- When a chip-select is asserted and the current segment is transmit-only or bidirectional:
  - in standard speed, only serial data line 0 is enabled as an output;
  - in dual speed, serial data lines 0 and 1 are enabled as outputs;
  - in quad speed, serial data lines 0 through 3 are enabled as outputs.
- When a chip-select is asserted and the current segment is receive-only or dummy, all serial-data output enables shall be off, regardless of speed.

---

## 8. Data-Path Control Behavior

The module provides strobes that control when data is written into the serializing path, when received data is read out, when the serial data shifts, and when the incoming serial data is sampled.

### 8.1 Write Strobes

For each byte-time in a transmit-only or bidirectional segment, the module shall issue a write strobe to request the next byte to transmit.

Write strobes shall not be issued during receive-only or dummy segments.

### 8.2 Read Strobes

For each byte-time in a receive-only or bidirectional segment, the module shall issue a read strobe when a received byte is complete and ready to be transferred out of the serial data path.

Read strobes shall not be issued during transmit-only or dummy segments.

### 8.3 Last-Byte Indications

When the module issues the write strobe for the final byte of a transmit segment, it shall also assert a last-write indication. This informs the transmit side that no further bytes will be needed for this segment.

When the module issues the read strobe for the final byte of a receive segment, it shall also assert a last-read indication. This informs the receive side that this byte completes the segment.

Last-byte indications shall only be asserted together with the corresponding write or read strobe, and shall be suppressed while stalled.

### 8.4 Shift Strobes

The module shall issue shift strobes at the serial-clock edges that advance the serial data lines.

The amount of data shifted per strobe depends on the active speed:

- standard: one bit;
- dual: two bits;
- quad: four bits.

### 8.5 Sample Strobes

The module shall issue sample strobes at the point in the serial-clock cycle where incoming serial data should be sampled.

The sample timing shall follow the configured clock phase:

- For phase 0, data is typically shifted out on the trailing edge and sampled on or near the leading edge.
- For phase 1, data is typically shifted out on the leading edge and sampled on or near the trailing edge.

When full-cycle sampling is enabled, the sample strobe shall be delayed by one additional serial-clock half-period relative to the normal sample point. This gives the remote device extra time to drive valid data.

### 8.6 Phase Alignment

The clock-phase setting shall only change the alignment of the data strobes relative to serial-clock edges. The module shall delay byte-start and byte-end events by one half-period when phase 1 is selected instead of phase 0, so that transmitted data and received-data sampling occur on the correct serial-clock edges.

---

## 9. Flow Control and Stall Behavior

The module receives ready signals from the transmit data source and the receive data sink.

### 9.1 Transmit Stall

If the module needs to request a byte for transmission, but the transmit data source is not ready, the module shall:

- assert the transmit stall indicator;
- suppress the write strobe and last-write indication;
- hold the serial clock and all other state;
- resume only when the transmit data source is ready.

### 9.2 Receive Stall

If the module has a completed received byte to transfer, but the receive data sink is not ready, the module shall:

- assert the receive stall indicator;
- suppress the read strobe and last-read indication;
- hold the serial clock and all other state;
- resume only when the receive data sink is ready.

### 9.3 Stall Effects

During any stall condition:

- no serial-clock edges shall be generated;
- no chip-select transitions shall occur;
- no write, read, sample, or shift strobes shall be presented;
- no command shall be accepted;
- all counters and progress tracking shall freeze.

A stall is a temporary pause, not an error condition. Normal operation shall resume automatically when the required data or sink space becomes available.

---

## 10. Command Acceptance and Status Indication

### 10.1 Command Ready

The module shall assert command ready whenever it is able to accept a new command segment.

Command ready shall be asserted:

- in the initial idle state;
- in the chip-select-active idle state, if the pending command selects the same chip-select and can continue without deasserting the chip-select;
- after the normal trail and idle closeout of a transaction, when the module is ready for the next command;
- at the end of a chip-select-held segment, if the next command for the same chip-select is already pending.

Command ready shall be suppressed during a stall.

A command shall only be accepted when the command-valid indication is asserted and the module drives command ready.

### 10.2 Active Indication

The active output shall indicate that the module is currently performing a command-related operation, such as:

- chip-select lead timing;
- serial-clock generation;
- chip-select trail timing;
- idle timing between transactions;
- configuration-switch delay.

The active output shall be low in the initial idle state. It shall also be low while the module is waiting in the chip-select-active idle state, even though a chip-select may be asserted low, because no command is currently being processed.

### 10.3 Full-Cycle Indication

The module shall provide a current full-cycle-mode indicator to the data path. This indicator shall reflect whether the active configuration uses full-cycle sampling. It shall be valid during command execution and shall be stable while data is being shifted or sampled.

---

## 11. Invalid Command Constraints

The module assumes that valid command descriptors are supplied.

The following conditions are not valid:

- a bidirectional segment at dual or quad speed;
- a reserved speed encoding;
- a chip-select ID that is greater than or equal to the number of chip-select lines.

The module is not required to produce defined SPI bus behavior for these invalid inputs. It may include assertions to flag such conditions during simulation.
